clue.text: Disturbance disruptively direct and not limited

parts.note: unrest is a state of public disturbance or agitation

indicators.note: disruptively says the letters of the following word are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a riot that broke out in a way both disruptive and unrestrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbance' reads as the subject of the sentence but supplies the opening letters; 'disruptively' works on the word after it, not on the disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no restrictions placed on it is free of limits, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Free one in France afflicted Switzerland

parts.note: un is the French word for one
hit can mean struck or afflicted, as a region hit by drought
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A free spirit, once in France, came down with something in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a horse or trailer from its hitch is to set it loose, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gem of a woman will be in Rugby Union next

parts.note: by can mean next to or beside, as in 'sit by me'

explanation.surface: A woman described as a real gem is about to join a rugby union team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a woman' hints that the gem is also a girl's name; 'will be in' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A red precious stone of corundum, one example of a gem.

clue.text: Fabric — possibly it's a mesh?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the words before it may be rearranged

parts.note: a net is an open mesh of threads

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a particular fabric counts as a mesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ITSA into SATI, followed by NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, glossy cloth imitating satin, so a kind of woven material.

clue.text: Sellers maybe supporting organised capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits below it, so it comes second

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it, past tense ran
Peter Sellers was one of the Goons, from the British radio comedy The Goon Show

explanation.surface: Salesmen, perhaps, are backing an organised effort in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' looks like salespeople but is the comedian Peter Sellers, a Goon on BBC radio's The Goon Show. Rangoon was the capital of Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, was long the seat of government of Burma (Myanmar), a capital city.

clue.text: Intimidate with line in monastic wear

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate or subdue them

explanation.surface: Monks are being bullied into wearing a certain garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded garment worn by monks, so an item of monastic clothing.

clue.text: Raise English veal to be cooked by the heartless

indicators.note: veal to be cooked suggests the meat's letters are prepared differently, that is rearranged
heartless says the middle letter is removed from the word it describes

explanation.surface: A recipe direction: English veal is to be cooked by an uncaring chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cooked' rearranges VEAL into LEVA; 'heartless' takes the middle H out of THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something to a higher position is to elevate it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Doing some calculations about daft Kate's ice show

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around another, here the reshuffled name

parts.note: figuring means working out sums or calculating

indicators.note: daft suggests the letters of the name are scrambled into a silly order

explanation.surface: Someone is busy doing sums about Kate's silly ice spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing some calculations' looks like a description of the skater, but it is the outer piece; the possessive in Kate's is fodder, giving its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Skating that traces patterns and performs jumps is a spectacle on ice, put on as a show.

clue.text: Remove name from flash illumination

parts.note: to strip is to remove, as in stripping paint

indicators.note: name from flash means the letter for name is taken away from the word for flash

parts.note: a flash of lightning

explanation.surface: An order to take a name off a flashing light display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove' gives the first word on its own; 'name from flash' then reads as an instruction: take the name's letter out of the bolt of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Long fluorescent tubes giving light are a form of illumination.

clue.text: To restrict popular greeting was effective

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
hi is an informal greeting
brakes or a measure that bit took hold and worked

explanation.surface: A popular greeting proved its worth as a way to hold someone back.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhibit is to hold back or curb, a verb synonym of restrict.

clue.text: Felt this could be a political grouping?

parts.note: the clue's word felt is what you get from the second word of the answer made new, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels this might make a political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'new' as an anagram signal working on LEFT gives FELT, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The radical movement of the 1960s on the political left was a political faction.

clue.text: Some account overdue as far as one can see

definitions.text: as far as one can see

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A creditor glances at a long overdue account.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside accoUNT Overdue. The definition plays on the old phrase 'unto the horizon'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic preposition meaning up to or until, so marking a limit reached.

clue.text: Objective pursued by old women to provide funds

indicators.note: pursued by says the first piece is followed by what comes next

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A goal chased by elderly ladies who want to raise money.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money to found or support an institution.

clue.text: Notice, in West Indies, a watercourse

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A traveller spots a stream in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry river bed in desert regions that runs with water after rain.

clue.text: A couple of thousand on up and up, done properly

indicators.note: in a down clue the second up says the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, so a couple is two of them
up means risen or out of bed

explanation.surface: A two-thousand-point rise, then another rise, all handled correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'up' is a piece (risen), the second turns everything round, as fits a down clue read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka is Anglo-Indian slang for genuine or first-class, so done the right way.

clue.text: Reduced power unit in ship leads to strikes

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: reduced says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: the watt is the unit of power

explanation.surface: Cutting a ship's power leads to industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' just joins wordplay and definition; 'strikes' is a plural noun, blows, not industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Swats are sharp slaps or blows, so strikes as nouns.

clue.text: displaying tailpipe?

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'displaying tailpipe? (7)': the clue begins lower case and is cut short, with no wordplay for EXHAUST; a search found no fuller text.

clue.text: Take lead, perhaps, in policy implemented by Roosevelt?

definitions.text: Take lead, perhaps, in policy implemented by Roosevelt?

parts.words: Take lead, perhaps, in policy implemented by Roosevelt?
parts.note: a fresh deal of the cards, or the word lead shuffled anew, alongside the 1930s American recovery programme

explanation.walkthrough: Taking a new lead could be shuffling LEAD afresh into DEAL; Roosevelt's 1930s reform programme carries the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin Roosevelt's 1930s programme of economic recovery and reform carried this name.

clue.text: Do this down to conform in a joint

definitions.meaning: to ... down or under is to submit and toe the line

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb knuckle under means submit, and the noun names a finger joint, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Work out with a French composer

parts.note: un is the French for a
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: Solving a puzzle with the help of a French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel a mystery is to solve or work it out.

clue.text: Pressing English team to take on a gentleman

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a side in cricket or football
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: An urgent need for the England side to take on a gentleman player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take on' just joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means urgent or demanding, so pressing.

clue.text: Judge over the top in key note

parts.note: G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A judge goes too far in a key memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is not 'important' but a musical key, here G.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotting is a brief written note.

clue.text: Music entrances copper, one in bath

indicators.note: read as en-trances, it means goes around, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: jazz is a style of music
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Music enchants a policeman, one relaxing in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrances' is not 'enchants' but 'goes round'; 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacuzzi is a brand of whirlpool bath.

clue.text: Warriors yet upset by lack of reverence

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors

indicators.note: upset says the letters of yet are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Fighters are nevertheless disturbed by disrespect.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPI is Zulu, a crossword regular for warriors; 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Impiety is irreverence or a lack of piety.

clue.text: Ripped up note about other ranks

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A ripped-up memo about the rank and file.
explanation.definitionFit: Tore is the past tense of tear, as in tearing a paper to pieces.

clue.text: Fix central heating in crisis

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or fix
CH is the abbreviation for central heating, used in British property listings

explanation.surface: Repairing the heating system in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinch is a moment of need, as in 'at a pinch', a critical situation.

clue.text: Argument suggesting water outlets should be withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn, drawn back, says the word for water outlets is read backwards

parts.note: taps let water out

explanation.surface: A quarrel suggests the taps ought to be taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be withdrawn' turns TAPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel.

clue.text: Spirit shown by bachelor at carnival venue

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is famous for its carnival

explanation.surface: A single man shows verve at the carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or liveliness, so spirit.

clue.text: Starts both leaders off providing drinks

indicators.note: both leaders off says the first two letters are removed

parts.note: begins means starts

explanation.surface: Getting under way, both team captains leave to get drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both leaders off' takes BE from BEGINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gins are measures of juniper spirit, so drinks.

clue.text: Blunder with a vehicle over in old kingdom

indicators.note: over says the whole run of pieces is turned back

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A driving mishap in an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: Navarre is a region of northern Spain that was once an independent kingdom; 'over' here turns the whole run, not just the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Navarre was a medieval kingdom straddling the Pyrenees.

clue.text: Former African or Asian leader in Ezra, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the pieces may be rearranged into another form
leader says take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An African or Asian leader appears in the Book of Ezra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives A from Asian; 'perhaps' rearranges A, IN and EZRA. Zaire is the old name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Zaire, the former name of the Congo, so an African of an earlier era.

clue.text: Vampire apt to be so cruel?

definitions.meaning: a vampire craves blood, so is naturally thirsty for it

explanation.definitionFit: A vampire literally thirsts for blood, and figuratively the word means savage or murderous.
